clue.text: Have Edward put under devilish control?

parts.note: to have something is to possess it
Ed is the usual short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man called Edward has been placed under a demon's spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seized by a demon or evil spirit is said to be possessed, ruled by that spirit's will.

clue.text: Expert in demonstration

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Expert in demonstration' (5): PRO (expert) and the definition 'demonstration' fit PROOF, but nothing gives the OF; the 'in' cannot supply it, so a word looks misread or missing and no blog or reprint was found.

clue.text: Source of energy suitable for enlightened prison

parts.note: solar means relating to the sun, the thing that lights up, so a solar room suits those who want to be lit
a cell is the room a prisoner is held in

explanation.surface: A clue playing on a prison room fit for the enlightened, as if a cell for sages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlightened' is read literally as lit up by the sun, which is what SOLAR describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A photovoltaic panel unit turns sunlight into electricity, so it supplies power.

clue.text: Delivery of fast-moving charged particle

parts.note: an express train or service is a fast one
an ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A physics phrase about how a speedy charged particle is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is the manner of speaking, as in an actor's delivery of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the manner in which words are spoken or conveyed, an actor's tone and phrasing.

clue.text: Cunning little reported

indicators.note: reported tells us we want a word that is said the same as the clue word's synonym

parts.note: slight means small or little

explanation.surface: A gossip passes on a small piece of cunning they heard about.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skilful trickery or dexterity, as in sleight of hand, so it is a kind of cunning.

clue.text: Modest quality of declaration by encyclopaedia

parts.note: dec. is a standard abbreviation of declaration (and declared, in cricket scores)
ency. is a dictionary abbreviation of encyclopaedia

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a humble trait found in a statement made by a reference work.
explanation.definitionFit: Decency is propriety and seemliness, the virtue of behaving modestly and respectably.

clue.text: Zero success initially for church service

parts.note: none means not any, that is zero

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word success

explanation.surface: A church service at which no one at all succeeds at first.
explanation.walkthrough: NONES is one of the canonical hours of prayer, said at the ninth hour of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: In the monastic daily round of prayer, nones is the office said in the early afternoon.

clue.text: Certainly not an expression of delight from a flood victim?

parts.note: no is a flat refusal, certainly not
ah is an exclamation of pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone caught by rising water refuses firmly yet sighs with pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the Biblical ark builder lived through the deluge rather than drowning in it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch of the ark was caught up in the great deluge, a person the flood struck.

clue.text: Wrongly described as

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Wrongly described as' (5): an anagram of INTER would give the letters, but the clue holds neither that fodder nor a definition of saltpetre; it is cut short and no reprint or blog was found.

clue.text: Team will need easily portable car component

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
something light is easy to carry

explanation.surface: A team will need some vehicle part that is easy to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lamp at the front edge of a motor vehicle, used as a parking lamp, is one of its parts.

clue.text: Neat border displaying woodland primula

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A tidy flowerbed edge showing a woodland flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like the adjective tidy, but it is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild spring flower of the Primula genus that grows in damp woods.

clue.text: Was charming, arranging the dance around noon

indicators.note: around says the rearranged words go round the letter for noon
arranging means the letters of the words the dance are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A host was delightful, organising the dance at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' shuffles the clue's two words into ENCHATED, and 'around' puts those letters round N. 'Was charming' reads as a past verb: the answer means charmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to charm or delight, so the past form stands for having charmed someone.

clue.text: Fine green one, possibly goddess?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fine green one, possibly goddess?' (4,6): FINE GREEN plus I (one) rearranged gives the letters, but 'goddess' does not define a fire appliance and looks misread; no blog or reprint was found.

clue.text: A loud measure of sound without liberal warning?

parts.note: the bel is a unit of sound intensity, ten decibels

explanation.surface: Asks whether a noisy sound level, minus a political liberal, could be an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer without L (liberal) is BEL, a unit of sound, and a ringing one is loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing alarm or chime is a signal that alerts people, as a fire alarm does.

clue.text: In French a short course of study is not paying

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: economics is a subject studied at school or university

explanation.surface: In France, a brief course turns out to be unprofitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the final S from ECONOMICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that does not make a profit is uneconomic: it costs more than it earns.

clue.text: Produce too much copy about some tennis

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fighting over money
a set is a unit of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Writing too many reports about a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, to overset is to set more type than will fit the space.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetting term for composing more text than the page can take.

clue.text: Convenient work for Spanish melody

parts.note: op., short for opus, is a musical work
por is Spanish for for
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A handy piece written for a Spanish song.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at a well-timed, suitable moment.

clue.text: Pulling along any poor leader

indicators.note: poor suggests the word any is badly formed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a king is a ruler or leader

explanation.surface: An inadequate ruler drags along anyone at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull sharply, so tugging hard is yanking.

clue.text: Silly about graduate in peculiar way of speaking

indicators.note: about says the word for silly goes round the graduate's letters

parts.note: idiotic means silly
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Mocking a graduate with a strange manner of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language follows usage particular to a tongue rather than logic, a speech form natives use.

clue.text: Be inquisitive about sick circle's ridicule

indicators.note: about says the nosy word goes round the others

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy
ill means sick
O has the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: Being nosy about an ailing group invites mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillory someone is to expose them to public scorn, as the old wooden stocks did.

clue.text: Ox eating quiet mother's veil

indicators.note: eating means the animal's letters surround the others, as if swallowing them

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired Tibetan ox
sh is a call for silence
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An ox chews up a quiet mother's veil.
explanation.definitionFit: The yashmak is a face covering worn by some Muslim women in public.

clue.text: One pedalling machine in Cyprus about to tilt over

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
c., for circa, means about
to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A rider in Cyprus about to fall over sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone who works the pedals of a bicycle, the machine being a bike.

clue.text: a line from circle of light

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'a line from circle of light' (7): CORONA (circle of light) plus L (line) builds the letters, but the clue starts in lower case with no definition, so its opening is cut off and no reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: a line from circle of light

clue.text: Gets car going for men of 4 the cloth

explanation.surface: Clergy turning the key in a motor's ignition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rev an engine is to run it fast to start off; Revs, short for Reverends, are clergy.

clue.text: Is one in television up to what caller can do?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the built word is read from bottom to top
in places the earlier words inside the letters for television

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a single person on screen is equal to what a phone caller can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ISI inside TV, giving TISIV, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller is a visitor, someone who drops in, so calling on a person is paying a call.

clue.text: One following movement of star and moon with little hesitation?

indicators.note: movement of says the words star and moon are moved about into a new order

parts.note: er is the small sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A stargazer who tracks the heavens, pausing only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the scientist, who follows the motions of heavenly bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies the heavens follows, that is tracks, the motions of stars and planets.

clue.text: Change direction when up before English law officer

indicators.note: before puts the turned word ahead of the English letter
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to veer is to swerve or change course

explanation.surface: An English officer turns round as he climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a local magistrate or official in old England.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England this was a manorial or shire magistrate who enforced the law locally.

clue.text: Show open disobedience being fed up with the unknown

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with not knowing rebels openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like annoyed, but 'up' turns FED round.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy is to resist authority openly and boldly.

clue.text: Provincial result changes island

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word result are altered into a new order

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An election result alters an island community.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Irish province Ulster is a person from that province.

clue.text: Encountered with reference to verse?

parts.note: met is the past of meet, encountered
re means concerning, with reference to

explanation.surface: A remark that someone was met over a matter of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: metre is the rhythm of verse rather than verse itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the rhythmic pattern of stressed syllables that marks lines of poetry.

clue.text: Beheading soldier guarding the gate could ensure it

definitions.text: Beheading soldier guarding the gate could ensure it

indicators.note: beheading means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier posted on guard at a gate

explanation.surface: Killing the guard at the gate would get you in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: cut the sentry's head off and you are free to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the guard would secure access, the way in to a place.

clue.text: Lightweight bike having production run of 1000?

parts.note: a kilo is a unit of weight, a lightish one
a cycle is a bike

explanation.surface: A light bicycle made in a batch of a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: A kilocycle is a thousand cycles, an old unit of frequency; the surface pretends it is a batch of a thousand bikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The old frequency unit means a thousand oscillations, so a thousand repeated runs.
